name: @projexlight/sdk-service-request
summary: Service-request ticketing primitive for ProjexCloud: queue + routing-rule + ticket + assignment workflow that sits between intake (web form, email-in, conversational) and execution (sdk-dispatch / sdk-assignment / sdk-workflow). The 'help me with X' surface that any internal-ops or customer-support blueprint pulls in.

endpoints.description: Fetch a ticket + transition history + linked execution refs.
Assign a ticket to a persona / queue.
Advance ticket state (open → in-progress → resolved → closed).
Create or update a queue + its routing rules.

events.name: service_request.ticket.created.v1
events.description: Ticket created; carries intake-channel + initial classification.

events.name: service_request.ticket.assigned.v1
events.description: Ticket assigned to a persona / queue.

events.name: service_request.ticket.sla.breached.v1
events.description: Ticket crossed its SLA deadline; downstream alerts.

events.name: service_request.routing.rule.fired.v1
events.description: Routing rule matched + routed a ticket.

models.description: Per-queue row: name, default_assignee, sla_minutes, routing_rules.
Per-rule row: queue_id, predicate, priority, target.
Per-ticket row: requester_persona, kind, state, sla_deadline, assigned_to.

hooks.name: createTicket
hooks.description: Service entry. Auto-routes via configured rules unless explicit queue specified.

hooks.name: assignTicket
hooks.description: Assign a ticket; refuses if persona is not a member of the queue.

hooks.name: transitionTicket
hooks.description: Advance state; refuses transitions outside the configured graph.

hooks.name: createQueue
hooks.description: Create / update a queue + its routing rules.

hooks.name: startSlaSweeper
hooks.description: Background worker: emits .sla.breached.v1 for tickets past deadline.

scenarios.title: Customer submits a help form → ticket created
scenarios.when_to_use: Webform intake; auto-route to the right queue based on the configured rules.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Ticket row + auto-routed to billing queue per rule. Emits .ticket.created.v1 + .routing.rule.fired.v1.

scenarios.title: Inbound chat thread auto-opens a ticket
scenarios.when_to_use: Reactive on conversation.session.opened.v1 with kind='support' — open a ticket so the support team has a tracked work item even if the chat moves async.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Ticket opens linked to the conversation thread. Support agent sees both in the same view.

scenarios.title: Sweeper fires alert when ticket crosses SLA
scenarios.when_to_use: Background worker checks every 60s; tickets past their SLA deadline fire .sla.breached.v1 → sdk-notification routes to the queue manager.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Breach event fires once per ticket (idempotent). Notification escalates to the manager + the customer-success oncall.

scenarios.title: Supervisor reassigns a stalled ticket
scenarios.when_to_use: Ticket stuck on rep who's OOO; supervisor reassigns to another rep in the same queue.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Assignment row updated; emits .ticket.assigned.v1 with reason + supervisor pinned for audit.

scenarios.title: Ticket resolves with a link to the executed action
scenarios.when_to_use: Rep resolved by issuing a refund via sdk-payment; the ticket transition carries the refund ref so audit chain links cause + effect.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Ticket closes; emits .ticket.transitioned.v1. Execution refs visible in the ticket detail for SOC2 audit traceability.

compliance_posture.notes: Ticket body is PII; permission filtering via sdk-rebac. Resolution refs link tickets to the actual SDK actions taken so a SOC2 auditor can replay cause→effect. SLA-breach events are the SOC2-CC7.1 monitoring artifact.
